rounds.text: LEEL Electricals Ltd is currently trading at a profound disconnect from its underlying asset base, evidenced by a price-to-book ratio of 0.10x [E2]. This extreme valuation gap is paired with a P/E ratio of 3, suggesting that the market has failed to price in the company's recent operational turnaround [E1]. The business has demonstrated a massive shift in performance, moving from a -40% operating margin three years ago to a 12% margin in the trailing twelve months [E16]. This recovery is further validated by a 2602% compounded sales growth rate over the trailing twelve months and a 766% year-over-year sales increase [E8, E49]. While the company is showing signs of renewed profit growth exceeding 20% year-over-year, it is important to acknowledge that the long-term historical trend remains challenging [E7, E52]. Conceded: [E4], [E5], [E6], [E7], [E17].

The bull’s reliance on a 0.10x price-to-book ratio [E2] and a 3x P/E [E1] ignores that these metrics are symptoms of a company in long-term terminal decline rather than a mispriced opportunity. The 10-year compounded sales growth of -36% [E7] confirms that the business has been systematically destroying value for a decade, rendering the recent TTM sales spike [E8, E49] an outlier rather than a sustainable trend. Furthermore, the operating margin has already begun to contract, falling from 20% in the year-ago quarter to 11% in June 2026 [E17], which directly undermines the narrative of a permanent operational turnaround [E16]. With an ROCE of 2.3% and an ROE of 2.2% [E5, E6], the company is failing to generate meaningful returns on its capital, explaining why the market assigns it a negligible ₹ 10.1 Cr valuation [E3]. The absence of any dividend yield [E4] further signals that shareholders are receiving no tangible return for the risks associated with this volatility. Conceded: [E8], [E16], [E49], [E52].

Operating margin is 12% in TTM against -40% three years earlier (+52 percentage points).
Quarterly operating margin is 11% in Jun 2026 against 20% in the year-ago quarter (-9 percentage points).
Screen reason (bull side): strong sales growth
